questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me to be able to go to a country/university I found interesting but which also had courses I would like.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but some things were difficult because I felt some information could have been combined information instead of separate.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, other than Residential Assistents at the place I was living.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy in the sense of the university letting you know it was a possibility, but it did feel like having to go through the hunger games in order to secure an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived off campus but still among other people. So, it is important to say that it can be a very social thing!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has nothing to do with the university itself, the building I was living in just had multiple severe issues like four times having no heating during winter (for multiple days).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I felt like you had to go through different websites in order to register: finding the courses on university website, apply for it in one 'back end' system, and having the actual student website (similar to Absalon) a completely third place. Again, I feel like having one system (like KUnet) for this would be much easier. Many times during the registration process (and just the application process for both UCPH and Leiden) I felt lost and confused.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None that I was aware of.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not able to do two specific courses because it would clash with my ECTS points, but I did get into the classes I wanted regardless.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time! Don't rush the process, it can take some time to understand and find information.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My classes were on something called 500 'level', what that means I do not know. But, personally I felt very satisfied with the level of my courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference was that all three of my courses were split between two professors. It did not bother me, but I do prefer having just one professor and their style of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Core course 1: Critical perspectives in Art History & Musuem Studies, 2) Interculturality: Key concepts, 3) Popular Music: Pleasure, Ideology, Technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The third one, Popular Music: Pleasure, Ideology, Technology! The professors were really proficient and the syllabus was really interesting. I also find it extremely interesting to research and analyze how something as broad as music can have an impact culturally.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Fees on paying for housing. Twice I had to pay 400 DKK extra to pay my rent because I payed with my Danish bank account. I would recommend getting a local bank account, transfer from the Danish into the local one, and then pay with that one after!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive. Denmark is one of the most expensive countries in the world, so for me it was cheaper to live in the Netherlands.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know as I didn't join any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know there were quite a lot especially with ESN (Erasmus Student Network, and they had a Whatsapp group where they sent information). At the institution itself there was also things you could join, however for a price. I wanted to join an afterschool activity, but ultimately opted out because of the cost.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know as I didn't join any. I wanted to do drama though!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to see other cities in the country! I was lucky enough to live in a town where it was easy and close to go to other cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the Dutch culture is very like the Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your class! I was also living in a place where other students were living, and I ended up socializing more with them than my classmates. So, I'm a little bummed I didn't spend more time socializing with my classmates, even though I still managed to get friends from there!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was no cultural challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it reminded me so much of the Danish culture, it made me feel at home away from home!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Like I mentioned before, the process for applying can be difficult to navigate in, so remember to do your deadlines within a good timeframe. 2) Do the introduction week! It makes it easy to meet new people and see what the school has to offer. 3) Remember to enjoy yourself as well as doing your academic work. To have fun and explore the culture, to me, is just as much a part of the exchange as the schooling is.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have money saved up for when/if you get housing through the university! I thought you would have to pay at a later date, but I actually had to pay what I think was around 21.000 DKK in June (first month + the last two months of rent, I think).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting the opportunity to get away for a semester, and stand on my own two feet alone. In Denmark most of us are used to living with roomies, but by going on this exchange I was able to live alone and experience this for the first time in my life. I also had great and interesting courses that taught me new things, and of course the friends I made doing my stay!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had some personal challenges during my exchange, but otherwise it was an amazing experience!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it if it is possible for you to go!!! It is a once in a life time experience, and I am really happy I did it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
